key_insight: B-VQE extends variational quantum eigensolvers to non-Hermitian many-body physics by optimizing independent left/right states and directly detecting exceptional points and biorthogonal phase transitions.
engineering_relevance: It offers a NISQ-friendly route to map open-system phase diagrams without ancilla-heavy post-selection, which could improve practical simulation of non-Hermitian materials and devices.
method: Uses separate variational circuits for left and right eigenstates of a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
Optimizes a biorthogonal objective with an Exceptional-Point Detector and Non-Hermitian Quantum Geometric Tensor readout.
Applies importance-sampling mitigation to reduce post-selection overhead and preserve polynomial scaling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on a non-Hermitian Hubbard chain, XXZ spin chain, and 2D (t)-(J) model, with relative energy errors below 5×10^-3 and accurate exceptional-point localization in noise-free simulations.
watch_item: Performance is shown primarily in simulations, so hardware noise, circuit depth, and the robustness of biorthogonal measurements on real NISQ devices remain key implementation risks.
paper_title: Exceptional-Point-Anchored Variational Quantum Eigensolver for Non-Hermitian Many-Body Phase Diagrams: Bridging Skin-Effect Topology and Entanglement Criticality on NISQ Hardware
